subject.title: [Feature]: Fallback approval mode + model attribution in messages

question: Should OpenClaw add a core opt-in approval gate before executing configured model fallbacks, and what config, timeout, denial, and channel-delivery contract should it use?
rationale: The remaining request changes fallback runtime behavior and adds config surface; repository policy treats fallback behavior and config additions as compatibility- and product-sensitive.

options.title: Design a default-off core gate
options.body: Define a per-agent or per-session approval contract with timeout behavior, channel delivery semantics, docs, and tests before implementation.

options.title: Keep fallback automatic
options.body: Treat current fallback notices plus response-prefix attribution as the supported visibility/control model and close the approval direction as not planned.

options.title: Route through extension design
options.body: Add or refine a plugin/API hook for approval decisions instead of adding a one-off model config key in core.

recommendation.title: Design a default-off core gate
recommendation.body: Define a per-agent or per-session approval contract with timeout behavior, channel delivery semantics, docs, and tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history route for fallback policy, config shape, and docs is steipete.
